close_reason: Landed option (b) on four sub-types per recommendation. Task.at_type intentionally not touched per partial-response analysis in close comment. Workspace propagation sweep filed as JMAP-ky8g.10. Commit a3cf20a.
description:
In crate-jmap-tasks-types/src/task.rs, the @type field is declared as required `String` on Person (line 53), CheckItem (line 82), Checklist (line 117), and Comment (line 142):

    #[serde(rename = "@type")]
    pub at_type: String,

but on Task itself (line 266) it is Option<String> with skip_serializing_if. The asymmetry is wrong, and the required-String form has a concrete failure mode.

Trigger: any deserialize input where a Person / CheckItem / Checklist / Comment object is missing @type. Examples:
  1. A spec-violating server response (vendors do ship these).
  2. A response built by serde_json::to_value on a partial sub-object.
  3. Hand-rolled fixtures, including the workspace's own future fixtures.

Actual behavior: serde returns "missing field `@type`" error and the entire Task deserialize fails. The user / contributor sees a deserialize error pointing at @type, which is non-obvious to debug because the docs frame @type as a discriminator the user should never have to think about.

Note: tests/types_test.rs fixtures and helpers (`task_with`, `task_list_with`) all currently set @type explicitly, so this is invisible from the test suite — the hazard is at the server / client integration boundary, not in unit tests.

Fix options (pick one, then apply uniformly across all four sub-types and the Task type itself):
  (a) Change to `Option<String>` with `default` and `skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none"` to match Task. Document that the @type discriminator is the producer's responsibility, the deserializer accepts absent.
  (b) Add a serde default that supplies the type-mandated string ("Person", "CheckItem", "Checklist", "Comment") when absent. Then it stays `String` but is always populated. This is the closer-to-spec form.

(b) is closer to RFC 8984 §1.4.1 intent and avoids breaking the existing typed value contract; it is the recommended fix.

Workspace propagation: same asymmetry exists in `crate-jmap-jscalendar-types` re-exports (Location, Participant, Alert, etc.) and in the calendars-types/contacts-types siblings — file a follow-up sweep bead if so.
title: Required @type on Person/CheckItem/Checklist/Comment breaks partial responses
